claim: Sec. 6 --- the two representations partition the competency questions, and must disagree about the cofactor

checks.check: the two views overlap on no question (measured)
checks.detail: of 13 questions: 4 signature-only, 6 chain-only, 0 both, 1 neither. Overlap fraction = 0.00. A large overlap would mean the views are redundant, not partitioned.

checks.check: block structure: group 1 signature-dominated, group 2 chain-dominated
checks.detail: group 1 (classification): signature 8 vs chain 2; group 2 (mechanism): signature 0 vs chain 9. The dominance reverses between groups, which is the block structure Table 1 claims.

checks.check: group 3 (context) was unanswerable by either view before the medium
checks.detail: all 3 context questions score 0 for the signature view; all 3 are supplied by the medium semantics. Without Sec. 3-4 every group-3 cell is empty in both columns.

checks.check: NEGATIVE CONTROL: the medium leaves questions unanswered
checks.detail: 3 question(s) remain below a full answer even after this paper: ['activation energy', 'thermodynamic properties', 'temperature, pressure, pH']. An extension that answered everything would be overclaiming.

checks.check: Prop. 6.2: two reactions differing in stoichiometry have identical chains
checks.detail: 'A + B -> C' and '2A + B -> C (A individuated once, used twice)' commit identical boundary (2.2200e-03), identical cut count (3), identical residues. A leaf individuated once and used twice is indistinguishable at the level of committed boundary, so the coefficient is not recoverable --- which is why the signature view needs an n-ary bridge node to carry it.

checks.check: Thm 6.3: the two views disagree about the cofactor
checks.detail: signature: NOT a participant (net coefficient 0). chain: IS individuated (carrier, cut once). Both correct --- they evaluate different predicates about the same molecule. A representation conflating them would be wrong in one of the two views.

signature_view.predicate: bears a net role in the transformation
signature_view.external_support: Rhea gives 4 participants for each of RHEA:19453/21824/17441; none is PLP

chain_view.external_support: PLP carries the amino group between half-reactions; deleting it deletes the mechanism (Cleland ping-pong bi-bi)

checks.check: NEGATIVE CONTROL: the views AGREE about a genuine participant
checks.detail: 2-oxoglutarate: signature says participant (net coefficient -1), chain says individuated (re-cut every turnover). The disagreement in Thm 6.3 is specific to carriers, not a general incoherence between the views --- without this check, Thm 6.3 could be explained by the two views simply never agreeing.

checks.check: Prop. 6.1 (SROIQ cannot express a residue chain)
checks.detail: This is a statement about the expressive power of the description logic underlying OWL 2, cited to Horrocks et al. (2006) and Baader et al. (2003). Establishing it requires a proof about SROIQ, not an experiment over this framework. No check here should be read as supporting it.
